lesson.title: Causes of World War I
lesson.summary: How alliances, militarism, imperial rivalry, and nationalism turned an assassination into a world war.
learningGoals: Explain the causes of World War I.
lesson.bigIdea: Long-term rivalries and rigid alliances turned a Balkan assassination into a war among the great powers.
lesson.context: Europe had avoided a general war for a century, but industrial power, colonial competition, and nationalism raised the stakes of every crisis.

sections.title: Long-term causes

blocks.text: Two alliance systems divided Europe: Germany and Austria-Hungary against France, Russia, and Britain. Militarism, the glorification of military power and the build-up of armies and navies, shaped planning. Germany and Britain raced to build battleships.
Imperial rivalries over colonies and nationalism in the Balkans raised tensions further.

blocks.title: Common trap
blocks.text: No single cause explains the war. Strong answers connect several causes and explain how they interacted.

sections.takeaway: Alliances, militarism, imperialism, and nationalism made a general war more likely.

sections.title: The July Crisis

blocks.text: On June 28, 1914, a Bosnian Serb nationalist assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary. Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia, Russia mobilized, and Germany declared war on Russia and France and invaded Belgium. Britain then entered the war.

blocks.title: Cause and effect
blocks.text: The assassination triggered an Austrian attack on Serbia, and alliance commitments and war plans then drew in the other great powers within days.

sections.takeaway: Alliances and mobilization plans spread a regional crisis into a world war.

connections.title: Imperial rivalry
connections.body: The competition for colonies described in Unit 6 created tensions among the powers that went to war in 1914.
connections.transferQuestion: How did imperial rivalry contribute to World War I?
connections.feedback: Name a rivalry between two powers and explain its effect.
